_comment: R8's entry hooks (docs/NATIVE_R8.md section 6.1), lifted beside config/insn_patches.json (tools/r8_lift.sh passes both). Each may decline: the lifted body then runs as before.

entry_hooks.note: the issue of one Bullet task (collision or solver): cellSpursCreateTask, then cellSpursQueuePushBody of its entry. A task whose work is native becomes a native job (port/native/phys_direct.cpp); any other is declined
the wait for one task of a manager: non-blocking cellSpursQueuePopBody round the slots. Done natively while the hooks are on (native completions, and the SPURS queues of lifted tasks)

The update (this, &dt) of the segmented boss's body segments (vtable 0x00FE4760 slot 8): its movement, turns and attack timing count frames (+0x75C, +0x770: one step a frame), so it ran 2 to 4.8 times too fast above the game's 30 fps. The gate calls it at 30 Hz with a step of 1/30 s (port/game_patches.cpp).

The update of the segmented boss's head (vtable 0x00FE4690 slot 8): it ignores the frame time and advances its object by a constant 1/30 s a call (the only update in the game that does), so above 30 fps it ran fast, and the body segments, which read positions from a trail the head fills, ran after it. The gate calls it at 30 Hz (port/game_patches.cpp).

The game's inflate of one map pack (.gz image r3, size r4, output r5), each through a SPURS instance, taskset, event flag, Edge LF queue and task of its own (func_005CF228). Done in the calling thread by port/native/inflate_direct.cpp; anything it does not recognise is declined to the lifted SPURS path.

The water's signal to its SPU task, cellSpursEventFlagSet(r3 + 0x3D400, r4): bit 0 once a simulation step (func_003C7460), bit 1 at shutdown (func_003C7AF4). With DOTHEROES_NATIVE_WATER=1 or sync the step is done natively (port/native/water_task.cpp); the quit and any other block are declined. Off by default; =check compares the lifted task's result with the native one.

The water's set-up (r3 the water): a SPURS instance 'Water', its taskset, a 0x3D600-byte block, an event flag and the SPU task. With native scheduling (DOTHEROES_NATIVE_WATER=1 or sync, the default) the port does the game's own stores and texture calls and no SPURS (port/phys_hooks.cpp, port/native/water_task.h); declined otherwise.

The water's shutdown: quit bit, the task's exit code, the taskset and instance torn down. Native when the set-up was (its markers in the globals): the worker's step finished, the globals cleared; declined for a real taskset.

The frame function that runs the waver (SPU image 2) while it is active. A test switch only: DOTHEROES_DEV_WAVER=<s>[,...] starts the waver at the hero's position at those times and times this function with it running and without (port/phys_hooks.cpp); the guard is 0 otherwise.

The waver's set-up (r3 = &{x, y, z}): a SPURS instance, taskset, block and event flag. Native by default (DOTHEROES_NATIVE_WAVER): the game's own stores and texture calls, markers in place of the SPURS objects (port/phys_hooks.cpp, port/native/waver_game.h); declined with =0 or =check.

The game's create-a-SPURS-task wrapper (r3 taskset, r4 block, r5 image), shared by the water and the waver: the waver's marker taskset runs a native frame on its worker; check mode notes the lifted waver's creations; everything else declined.
The game's wait-for-the-task wrapper (r3 block): the waver's marker block waits for the native frame; everything else declined.
The game's free-the-block wrapper (r3 block): nothing for the waver's marker; check mode compares the last lifted frame; everything else declined.
The game's destroy-the-taskset wrapper (r3 taskset): the waver's marker waits for the native frame and counts the teardown; everything else declined.
The game's finalize-the-instance wrapper (r3 instance): nothing for the waver's marker; everything else declined.
